title: Corpus intake: manifest schema, metadata stripping tool, storage rules
summary: Define how the Owner's raw scans reach the pipeline without ever entering git: a manifest, a metadata-stripping tool with tests, and the storage rules (VM path now, staging bucket after the Supabase AUTH).

acceptance_tests.test: services/reconstruction/corpus/README.md explains handover (Owner → gj-capture), the VM path, the staging-bucket path once Supabase exists, and the rule that raw media never enters git (CI repo-hygiene enforces it).

services/reconstruction/corpus/manifest.schema.json and manifest.json describe each capture: id, mode (room/tabletop), lighting, duration, device, object classes present (Bible §1 examples), readiness score + coverage summary (to match the live upload bundle, SPEC §3.1), notes; no GPS, addresses, or people.
acceptance_tests.evidence: files in PR; validate in test

acceptance_tests.test: services/reconstruction/tools/strip_metadata.py removes EXIF/GPS/XMP from JPEG and HEIC and location atoms from MP4/MOV (tests that inject synthetic GPS into generated fixtures and assert removal for all four formats are suggested).
requirements.txt pinned; pip-audit clean; lint green.

history.event: AUTH #003 applied: acceptance-criterion levels added; iOS-only wording
sharpened under AUTH #025 (capture UX): manifest carries readiness score + coverage summary so the corpus manifest and the live upload bundle share one shape (AT-2).

Implemented by gj-operator (direct commit to main): corpus/README.md (Owner capture guide + upload steps + Operator intake + storage/retention), manifest.schema.json + manifest.json (Bible §1 classes, Lego flag, readiness + coverage in the live-bundle shape, additionalProperties false, free-text PII rules; validated in CI), tools/strip_metadata.py (lossless ffmpeg remux / ExifTool, re-verified with ExifTool -ee + ffprobe) with fixture tests injecting synthetic GPS into JPEG, HEIC, MP4 and MOV, and a signed-link upload page + Modal intake app writing to the private gj-corpus Modal volume (deployed; E2E verified with synthetic media, then wiped). Storage deviates from AT-1's 'staging bucket' wording: staging Supabase is on the Free plan (50 MB per-object cap, 1 GB total), so the intake uses the Modal volume on the reconstruction account; a Supabase bucket needs a Pro upgrade (Owner decision). in-review for the non-automated AT-1 and that deviation. secondary-review: required (signed upload links).
